text.title: code-coverage Core Rules
text.summary: Eight testable rules for coverage as a CI gate: five on the gate itself and three that resolve the decision tree's run, block and skip branches.

rule.statement: Use branch coverage (`--cov-branch` / `--branches`) as the CI gate metric. Line coverage misses uncovered `else` branches on covered `if` lines.
rule.rationale: A test exercising the if-True path covers all if-line tokens, but the else branch is untested. Branch coverage requires both sides to execute.

rule.statement: Gate diff coverage (changed lines) at 90% via `diff-cover --fail-under=90 --compare-branch=origin/main`. Set repo total as a soft trend target (~80%), not a hard gate.
rule.rationale: Hard gates on repo total block PRs on codebases with legacy untested code. Diff gating locks new code without forcing full uplift at once.

rule.statement: Do NOT chase 100% repo coverage. Set 80-90% as the practical ceiling. The last 10-20% is defensive guards / error paths better validated by integration tests.
rule.rationale: Chasing 100% leads to testing trivial getters, mocking everything, and writing assertions that mirror implementation rather than verify behaviour.

rule.statement: Every CI run publishes `coverage.xml` as a PR artifact. PR comment summarises diff coverage % and the 3 largest uncovered branches.
rule.rationale: Reviewers cannot enforce coverage without seeing it. Artifact + summary comment makes the gate visible in PR review.

rule.statement: On modules tagged `critical` (auth, payments, RBAC), run mutation testing (mutmut / Stryker / cosmic-ray) weekly. Surviving mutants fail the job.
rule.rationale: Coverage % can be high while assertions are weak. Mutation testing kills the tests that pass even when the production code is wrong.

rule.statement: When every Applies-If holds (a runner that emits coverage.xml or an lcov report, CI on every PR, branch agreed as the metric, a known baseline repo-total branch percentage) and the record is producible, the run MUST be started by the trigger event named in Prerequisites (a new CI gate request, or a PR that lowered coverage) and MUST end in one output record with metric="branch", diff_coverage_pct measured by diff-cover --compare-branch=origin/main on the gated PR, repo_total_pct equal to the Step 2 baseline or its latest re-measurement, mutation_run_on_critical=true with critical_modules listing every module tagged critical, produced_by="code-coverage", an owner, and evidence pointing at the CI run URL that produced coverage.xml. scripts/validate-code-coverage.py MUST pass on that record before the gate is declared live.

rationale.source: diff-cover documentation (Bachmann); pytest-cov documentation, --cov-branch; Istanbul/nyc documentation, branch coverage

rule.rationale: The gate is only as real as the number it enforces: a record that names the metric, the diff-cover comparison branch and the CI run that produced coverage.xml lets a reviewer verify that the 90 percent figure came from branch coverage of the changed lines and not from a line-coverage report on main. Anchoring the run to a trigger and a run URL is what turns 'we have coverage' into a claim that can be checked when a regression slips through.

rule.statement: When the Applies-If conditions hold but a required field of the output record cannot be filled (no baseline repo-total branch percentage because Step 2 has not run, no coverage.xml because the runner emits only a terminal summary, no owner, no critical-module list when critical code exists), the run MUST stop before any gate is added to CI: no diff-cover step with a guessed --fail-under, no repo-total hard gate set to an unmeasured number, no record with metric="line" or a placeholder percentage. The block MUST name the missing Prerequisites row or procedure step (most often Step 2, baseline scan) and the tree is re-entered only after that artefact exists.

rationale.source: diff-cover documentation; coverage.py documentation, XML report

rule.rationale: A coverage gate installed without a baseline either blocks every PR on day one, after which the team disables it and never re-enables it, or is set so low that it enforces nothing; both outcomes are permanent because nobody revisits a gate that is already merged. Refusing the half-record and naming the baseline scan as the blocker costs one CI run and keeps the 90 percent diff gate credible when it does land.

rule.statement: When any Applies-If fails or any Skip-If trips (prototype with no stable suite, an integration-only suite on thin shims, or a codebase that is mostly generated migrations and admin boilerplate), no code-coverage record is produced and no coverage gate is added to CI. The skip MUST be written as a one-line decision that names the failing condition with its evidence (the test directory listing, the share of generated files, or the suite's integration-only marker) and routes the task to a Related methodology whose preconditions do hold, such as api-testing or django-pytest to build the suite first. A skip without a named condition and evidence is treated as unresolved.

rationale.source: Martin Fowler, 'TestCoverage'; Brian Marick, 'How to Misuse Code Coverage'

rule.rationale: Coverage on a thin integration shim or on generated boilerplate reports a high number that measures nothing, and a gate on it teaches the team that the metric is theatre; that lesson outlives the prototype. Recording why coverage was skipped, with the evidence, is what lets the gate be introduced later at the point the suite becomes worth measuring instead of being forgotten or reintroduced by someone who never saw the reason.
